props.gloss_en: any altar that lacks a ramp, or a horn, or a base, or squareness is unfit for the service
R' Yosei bar Yehuda: [an altar lacking] the surrounding ledge too [is unfit]
the drainpipes [of the altar] were created from the six days of creation
as it says: 'the curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of a craftsman's hands'
'the curves of your thighs' -- these are the drainpipes
'like jewels (chala'im)' -- that they are hollow (mechulalin) and descend to the deep
'the work of a craftsman's hands' -- this is the work of the craftsmanship of the Holy One, blessed be He
the school of R' Yishmael: 'bereshit' -- do not read bereshit but bara shit ('He created the pit')
R' Yosei: the drainpipes are hollow and descend to the deep
as it says (Isa 5:1-2): '...and he built a tower in its midst and also hewed out a vat in it'
'and he planted it with a choice vine' -- this is the Temple
'and he built a tower in its midst' -- this is the altar
'and also hewed out a vat in it' -- these are the drainpipes
there was a small gap between the ramp and the altar, on the west of the ramp
and once in seventy years the young priests go down there and gather from there congealed wine resembling cakes of pressed figs
and they come and burn it in sanctity
as it says (Num 28:7): 'in sanctity pour a libation of strong drink to the Lord' -- as its pouring is in sanctity, so its burning is in sanctity
libations: at first, one commits me'ila with them
once they have gone down to the drainpipes, one does not commit me'ila with them
(entertained) the ruling is R' Elazar bar Tzadok's, not the Rabbis'
for per the Rabbis they [the libations] have gone down to the deep -- [so what me'ila could there be?]
even if you say [it is] the Rabbis' -- [it speaks] where [the wine] was caught [before going down]
the ruling can be the Rabbis'
(entertained, second version) the ruling is the Rabbis', not R' Elazar bar Tzadok's
for per R' Elazar [bar Tzadok] they still stand in their sanctity -- [so me'ila should apply]
even if you say R' Elazar [bar Tzadok]: there is nothing whose mitzva has been performed with which one commits me'ila
the ruling can be R' Elazar bar Tzadok's
Reish Lakish: when they pour wine on the altar, they plug the drainpipes
to fulfil what is said: 'in sanctity pour a libation of strong drink (shekhar) to the Lord'
Rav Pappa: shekhar is a term of drinking, of satiation, of intoxication
Rav Pappa: learn from this that when a person is sated with wine, he is sated from his throat
Rava: a young scholar who has little wine should swallow it in gulps
Rava, over the cup of blessing, swallowed in gulps
Rava: 'how beautiful are your steps in sandals' -- how beautiful are the feet of Israel when they go up for the festival
'daughter of a prince (nadiv)' -- the daughter of Abraham our father, who is called nadiv
as it says (Ps 47:10): 'the princes of the peoples are gathered, the people of the God of Abraham'
'the God of Abraham' and not of Isaac and Jacob?! Rather: the God of Abraham, who was the first of the converts
the school of Rav Anan: 'the curves of your thighs' -- why are words of Torah likened to the thigh?
as the thigh is in concealment, so words of Torah are in concealment
R' Elazar (Micah 6:8): 'to do justice' -- this is judgment
'and to love kindness' -- this is acts of kindness
'and to walk modestly with your God' -- this is taking out the dead [for burial] and bringing a bride to the canopy
R' Elazar: greater is one who does charity than [one who offers] all the offerings
as it says (Prov 21:3): 'to do charity and justice is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice'
R' Elazar: acts of kindness are greater than charity
as it says (Hos 10:12): 'sow for yourselves by charity, reap according to kindness' -- one who sows may or may not eat; one who reaps certainly eats
R' Elazar: charity is rewarded only according to the kindness in it
as it says (Hos 10:12): 'sow for yourselves by charity, reap according to kindness'
the baraita: in three things acts of kindness are greater than charity
charity is with one's money; kindness both with one's person and with one's money
charity is for the poor; kindness both for the poor and for the rich
charity is for the living; kindness both for the living and for the dead
R' Elazar: whoever does charity and justice -- it is as though he filled the whole world with kindness
as it says (Ps 33:5): 'He loves charity and justice; the earth is full of the kindness of the Lord'
lest you say whoever comes to leap [to do it] leaps -- the verse says (Ps 36:8): 'how precious is Your kindness, O God'
one might think the same even of one who fears Heaven -- the verse says (Ps 103:17): 'the kindness of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him'
R' Chama bar Pappa: any person who has grace about him -- it is known that he fears Heaven
as it says (Ps 103:17): 'the kindness of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him'
R' Elazar (Prov 31:26): 'a Torah of kindness' -- Torah for its own sake is a Torah of kindness; not for its own sake, a Torah that is not of kindness
some say [R' Elazar said]: Torah [studied] to teach it is a Torah of kindness; not to teach it, a Torah that is not of kindness
